scope: Proposition 6.2 (Electrostatic potential, stress, and charge) of the manuscript “The Penrose inequality for maximal asymptotically hyperbolic initial data” (preprints/The-Penrose-inequality-for-maximal-asymptotically-hyperbolic-initial-data-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 641d4aa3892adbca), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 43. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every Me > 0 there is a weak solution u of divg E = 0, E = e(w) ∇u w , w = |du|g, u|S = −Me, u −→ 0 at infinity, (6.11) where E = 0 at w = 0. It satisfies −Me ≤ u ≤ 0, |u| + |du|g = O(r−1), and is C1,β locally up to S and in compactified coordinates (ρ, ω) up to ρ = 0, for some β > 0, where ρ = e−η. The continuous symmetric tensor Π = L(w)g − du ⊗ E♭ (6.12) is distributionally divergence free, is positive definite, and obeys (trg Π)2 − 2|Π|2 g = 3. (6.13) There is a continuous nonnegative function e0 on S2 such that, uniformly in angle, r2 |E|g −→ e0, r3(︁ Π(ν, ν) − 1 )︁ −→ −1 2e 3/2 0 . (6.14) Here ν points toward increasing r. The charge FMe = ∫︂ r=R g(E, ν) dAg (6.15) is independent of large R, satisfies FMe ≤ ∫︁ S2 e0 dAσ, and lim inf Me→∞ FMe ≥ A∗. (6.16)
